sources.entry: alacritty - A cross-platform, GPU-accelerated terminal emulator. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/jwilm/alacritty) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Alacritty is a fast, cross-platform, OpenGL terminal emulator that aims for sensible defaults with extensive configuration.
summary.what_it_does: Alacritty is a terminal emulator that runs on BSD, Linux, macOS and Windows. It is configured through a TOML file (alacritty.toml), searched in XDG config paths, $HOME, /etc, and %APPDATA% on Windows; documentation is provided as a man page (man 5 alacritty) and on the project website. It integrates with other applications rather than reimplementing their functionality, so it deliberately omits features such as tabs and splits, which the README says are better handled by a window manager or terminal multiplexer like tmux. The README states performance is measured with vtebench, and it notes that the project is at beta readiness and used as a daily driver by many. Precompiled binaries for macOS and Windows are available from GitHub releases, and other installs go through package managers.
use_cases: GPU-accelerated terminal on Linux, macOS or Windows
Pairing a terminal with tmux for multiplexing
how_to_run: Install via a package manager for your platform (see README installation section)
Or download a prebuilt binary from the GitHub releases page (macOS and Windows)
Create $HOME/.config/alacritty/alacritty.toml to configure (Alacritty does not create it automatically)
Read configuration docs with: man 5 alacritty
notable: GPU-accelerated OpenGL rendering with high throughput
Runs on BSD, Linux, macOS and Windows
TOML-based configuration with multiple standard config locations
Deliberately omits tabs and splits, leaving them to window managers or tmux
Precompiled binaries available on GitHub releases
caveats: README describes the software as beta, with some missing features and bugs
Requires at least OpenGL ES 2.0; Windows needs ConPTY (Windows 10 version 1809 or higher)
No built-in tabs, splits, or GUI config editor
